Course description

Chapter 1 of Casella and Berger: probability from first principles. We cover sets and sigma-algebras, Kolmogorov's axioms and what follows from them, counting, conditional probability and independence, random variables, distribution functions, and density and mass functions. Your pretest showed the calculations are solid, so this course spends its time on definitions and proofs. Every later chapter uses them.

You took the Chapter 1 pretest on October 6. Section 1.1 is skipped. The other sections teach only what the pretest showed was missing. The course ends with a one-page summary of the chapter and a chapter check.

Learning objectives

By the end of this course you can:

  1. State Kolmogorov's axioms and prove basic consequences from them alone, such as P(Aᶜ) = 1 − P(A), monotonicity, and Bonferroni's inequality.
  2. Count outcomes in the four sampling schemes (ordered or not, with or without replacement) and explain each formula.
  3. Tell pairwise from mutual independence, with a counterexample, and derive Bayes' rule, stating what it assumes.
  4. Explain what a random variable is (a function on the sample space) and what distribution it induces.
  5. State the three properties of a distribution function and prove that it is nondecreasing.
  6. Tell a mass function from a density, find a normalizing constant, and go between a density and its distribution function.

Texts

  • Required: Casella and Berger, Statistical Inference, 2nd ed. (Duxbury, 2002), Chapter 1, "Probability Theory", pp. 1–37. In your library.
  • Recommended: Patrick, Intermediate Counting and Probability (Art of Problem Solving; in your library), for extra counting practice if you want it.
  • Optional: Haigh, Probability: A Very Short Introduction (in your library), for history and intuition.
  • Not used: Ross, A First Course in Probability, because your copy is unreadable. Jaynes, Probability Theory, is saved for the Bayesian course.
